title: Small coiled rope basket
subtitle: A flat-bottomed basket made by coiling rope and joining with dc stitches.
excerpt: The coiled rope basket wraps rope in a spiral and joins the rounds with dc worked over the rope as a core. The dc anchors the rope coils together and adds colour.
sourceNotes: Coiled rope construction is a traditional basketry method adapted for crochet. No direct Weldon source. Contemporary documentation.

glossaryTerms.definition: Hold the rope core along the top of the previous round, insert hook over and around the rope, and complete a dc. The stitch encases the rope while simultaneously joining the new round to the previous one.
A slip stitch worked through both the current round of rope and the stitch of the previous round, holding the coil together at the base of each dc.
Threading yarn tails through stitches with the tapestry needle.

crochet.gaugeText: 8 dc-over-rope rows = 10 cm height; 1 round = approx 3 cm diameter added.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Round basket, 18 cm diameter, 8 cm tall.

content.text: A small coiled rope basket is 18 cm across and 8 cm tall.
DC stitches worked over a rope core
join each new coil to the previous round while wrapping the rope in a contrasting colour of DK cotton. The result looks like traditional coiled basketry.
Use approximately 10 m of thick cotton washing line or similar rope (5-6 mm diameter) and 50 m of DK cotton for the joining yarn. A 4 mm hook works the dc over the rope.
What you need
Starting the base
Coil the rope into a tight circle about 3 cm across. Work dc stitches all around the coil to lock the centre tight. Approximately 12 dc for the first coil.
Building rounds
For each new round: hold the rope coil next to the previous round. Work 1 dc over the rope and into the stitch of the previous round (
coil join
). Space the stitches so the rope curves naturally without gaps or bunching. Add extra dc over the rope between the join stitches on wider rounds to keep it flat.
Sides

After round 6 (approximately 18 cm diameter), stop adding extra dc between joins. Work dc over rope and into previous round only. The sides will naturally begin to rise. Continue for 6 more rounds (approximately 8 cm tall). Cut rope, tuck end inside last dc, secure with sl st.
Finishing
Secure yarn tail with
weaving in ends
. Trim rope end closely inside the basket.
Care
Spot clean. Do not machine wash rope baskets. Reshape while damp.
What to try next
The basic round basket uses the same dc-in-spiral technique without the rope core. Or try the oval basket for a larger coiled version.
